mercy_translation.text:
Those who disbelieve the resurrection set before themselves a great refutation of their own position: all the demons and the gods worshiped by them do not drive away the Christ whom they call dead; rather, Christ exposes all of them as dead.

For if it is true that a dead person accomplishes nothing, while the Savior daily accomplishes so much—drawing people to piety, persuading them toward virtue, teaching immortality, raising them to desire heavenly things, revealing knowledge of the Father, breathing into them power against death, showing himself to each person, and overthrowing the godlessness of idols—while the gods and demons of unbelievers can do none of these things, but rather become dead in the presence of Christ, their illusion rendered idle and empty; and if by the sign of the cross all magic ceases, every spell is rendered ineffective, idols are deserted and abandoned, irrational pleasure is brought to an end, and faith looks up from earth toward heaven—whom should one call dead? Christ who accomplishes so many things? But activity does not belong to the dead. Or should one call dead that which does nothing at all but lies lifeless, which is precisely the condition of demons and idols as dead things?

The Son of God, being living and active, works every day and carries out the salvation of all. Death, meanwhile, is daily shown to have been weakened, while idols and demons are shown rather to be dead. Therefore no one should any longer hesitate concerning the resurrection of his body.

Anyone who disbelieves the resurrection of the Lord's body seems not to know the power of the Word and Wisdom of God. For if he truly took a body to himself and made it his own according to the reasonable sequence already shown, what was the Lord to do with it? What end should the body have had once the Word had come upon it?

It could not avoid dying, since it was mortal and was being offered to death on behalf of all; for this reason the Savior had prepared it for himself. Yet it could not remain dead because it had become the temple of Life. Therefore it died as mortal, but came alive again because of the Life within it; and its works are the sign of the resurrection.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
The chapter contrasts the continuing activity of Christ with the inactivity expected of the dead.
The body dies because it is genuinely mortal but cannot remain in death because it is the temple of Life.
